analysis.investment_thesis: CapitalNumbers is a debt-free, high-ROCE (26.5%) digital engineering firm trading at just 8.9x P/E with a strong promoter holding of 74.67% — arithmetically cheap on paper. But revenue growth has collapsed from a 28% 5Y CAGR to just 2% in FY25, and operating profit actually declined, which tempers conviction in the India IT SME growth story.
key_strengths: Debt-free balance sheet with ROE 20% / ROCE 26.5% — high quality capital efficiency
Strong promoter skin in the game at 74.67%, zero borrowings
Cheap valuation: 8.9x P/E with 5/5 years positive OCF and ~11% FCF yield (18 Cr FCF / 203 Cr mcap)
key_risks: Growth stalling — revenue up only 2% (98→100 Cr) and operating income fell 34→30 Cr in FY25
Small-cap IT services export model vulnerable to global tech-spend slowdown and AI disruption of code-for-hire
Large IPO cash raise (equity jumped 67→171 Cr) with 77 Cr investing outflow — capital allocation of fresh cash unproven
red_flags: Sharp deceleration in FY25 revenue and operating profit despite prior 28%+ CAGR — possible structural issue
analysis.detailed_analysis: At first glance this ticks many of my boxes — promoter at 74.67%, zero debt, ROCE 26.5%, FCF-positive every year, and a 5-year net profit CAGR of 39%. Trading at 8.9x earnings for a business compounding earnings at that pace would normally be a screaming buy. The India digital-services export theme has real structural tailwinds, and CapitalNumbers has demonstrated it can grow 3x in five years with minimal capital.\n\nHowever, the FY25 numbers give me pause: revenue barely grew (98→100 Cr), operating income contracted (34→30 Cr), and the company raised a large chunk of equity (reserves 46→147 Cr) whose deployment is unproven — 77 Cr went into investing activities which at this scale could be treasury rather than growth capex. Small-cap Indian IT-services shops face genuine pressure from global tech-spend caution and generative-AI commoditizing bread-and-butter development work. I'd want to see two more quarters of growth reacceleration before sizing up. Watch-list with conviction to buy aggressively if growth resumes at 20%+; otherwise the cheap multiple may be a value trap.
